subject: Model gen-2x elevated error rates — customer-facing updates
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:13:22 -0700
Subject: Alert: gen-2x increased 5xx / timeouts (initial detection)

Heads up — monitoring just started alerting on a spike in 5xx and timeout errors for model 'gen-2x' serving in the us-west cluster.

Quick summary:
- Window: 09:00–09:10 PDT
- Error type: 502/504 and a subset of internal runtime panics
- Approx affected requests: ~720 requests, ~14% of gen-2x traffic in that window
- Upstream: NO change in customer prompts; traffic pattern consistent

Immediate actions taken:
- Scaled the gen-2x pod group by +20% (temporary)
- Enabled routing fallback to gen-1x for low-latency tier (policy: prefer gen-2x unless 5xx seen)
- Captured heap and worker logs for the affected nodes (/var/logs/gen2x/...)

Next steps I'm running now:
- Triage logs for obvious OOM/driver issues
- Run quick regression against recent kernel rollout (was pushed 48h ago)

I'm tagging Grace for CS coordination and Marissa for upstream account comms. Will update in ~1h or sooner if we have a mitigation.

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 10:05:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident affecting gen-2x model — immediate update and workaround

Alicia —

Thanks for the flag; we detected increased error rates on our gen-2x model earlier this morning and wanted to share what we know and what you can do immediately to reduce impact.

What happened (high level):
- A subset of gen-2x workers began returning transient 5xx / timeout errors starting ~09:00 PDT. Our monitoring shows ~12–15% of gen-2x traffic in us-west was affected during the peak.

What we’ve done so far:
- Scaled the affected pool and applied an automatic fallback policy to route new requests to gen-1x if gen-2x responds with 5xx.
- Isolated failing hosts and collected logs (we will share sanitized samples).

Recommended immediate workarounds for your team:
1) If you need stability over the next 6–12 hours, please switch model param to gen-1x (identifier: gen-1x-stable) — we will maintain identical API compatibility for the call shape.
2) Reduce max_sequence_length for long prompts where possible; this reduces exposure to the failing path.

We expect to have a more detailed technical update within 4 hours and will share a recovery estimate then. I’ll coordinate with Jonas and Marissa and keep this thread as the single source of truth.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your pipeline and will prioritize remediation.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: workaround-instructions.pdf (short steps to pin gen-1x and reduce sequence length)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 14:30:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident affecting gen-2x model — preliminary technical findings

Alicia / Grace / team —

Quick update with more technical detail (preliminary):

Findings so far:
- The error mode correlates with a regression in the attention kernel that was part of the 2026-07-09 runtime patch. Under certain batched request sizes and longer sequence lengths (>2k tokens), a race condition can trigger worker side exceptions leading to 502/504.
- Affected machines show elevated GC pauses and periodic worker restarts (we collected logs and a few core traces).

What we did (engineering):
- Rolled back the specific kernel change for the gen-2x pool in us-west; this reduced the error rate by ~80% in our synthetic tests.
- Reconfigured autoscaler thresholds to reduce burst-induced batching that surfaced the bug.

Customer impact and risk:
- Short-term: requests that hit the bad batching path may still see sporadic 5xx until the pool fully cycles (ETA: 2–4 hours).
- Medium-term: we’re preparing a tested patch that prevents the race; planned rollout target: 2026-07-13 02:00 UTC (after validation).

Attachments: gen-2x-fault-samples.log (sanitized), brief-trace-snippets.txt

I will follow up with the post-incident RCA and a timeline for the preventative patch. If Acme needs help switching models or updating client-side retry logic, we can schedule an on-call pairing session.

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 16:45:01 -0700
Subject: Resolved: gen-2x errors mitigated — post-incident summary and next steps

Alicia —

Update: the immediate incident window is over and gen-2x error rates have returned to baseline in us-west. Thank you for switching to gen-1x while we mitigated. Below is a concise post-incident summary and next steps; Jonas has attached the full postmortem.

What caused the incident (short):
- A regression in an attention kernel introduced on 2026-07-09 caused a race in the batched execution path under specific batch/sequence length combos, resulting in intermittent worker exceptions and 5xx responses.

Timeline recap:
- 2026-07-11 09:00 PDT — Monitoring alerts triggered for gen-2x 5xx spike
- 09:10 — Autoscale + fallback routing enabled
- 10:05 — CS notified customer and suggested gen-1x fallback
- 14:30 — Engineering identified kernel regression and rolled back change for gen-2x pool in us-west
- 16:00 — Error rate fell to baseline; continuing validation and healing

Customer impact and remediation offered:
- Impact window: ~09:00–16:00 PDT on 2026-07-11 (intermittent; peak ~12–15% of gen-2x requests)
- We will apply a proactive credit to Acme Analytics for the impacted usage window per our SLA. Marissa will follow up with the billing details and the HubSpot record.

Action items / next steps:
- Engineering will deploy a tested kernel patch to all regions on 2026-07-13 02:00 UTC (post-validation).
- We will share the full postmortem PDF (attached) and open a short remote session to review the patch and mitigation controls if you’d like.
- Recommend Acme keep gen-1x as a short-term fallback for any long-sequence workloads until the patch is live.

Attachments: gen2x-incident-postmortem.pdf

If you’d like, Marissa can coordinate the billing/credit details and schedule a 30-min technical review with Jonas next week.

Apologies again for the disruption — we value the trust you place in Redwood and will take measures to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
